readmeHtml:
The visual editor for React

Documentation • Puck AI • Demo • Discord

⭐️ Enjoying Puck? Please leave a star!


What is Puck?

Puck is an open-source visual editor for React. Build drag-and-drop interfaces with your own components.

Embed Puck as a React component in your existing application. You own your components and data, with no vendor lock-in.

Puck's MIT license permits internal and commercial use.

Quick Start

1. Install the package

npm i @puckeditor/core --save

2. Render the editor

// Editor.jsx
import { Puck } from "@puckeditor/core";

// Create Puck component config
const config = {
  components: {
    HeadingBlock: {
      fields: {
        children: {
          type: "text",
        },
      },
      render: ({ children }) => {
        return <h1>{children}</h1>;
      },
    },
  },
};

// Describe the initial data
const initialData = {};

// Save pages to your backend (see step 4)
const save = (data) => {};

// Render Puck editor
export function Editor() {
  return <Puck config={config} data={initialData} onPublish={save} />;
}

3. Render the page

// Page.jsx
import { Render } from "@puckeditor/core";

export function Page() {
  return <Render config={config} data={data} />;
}

4. Choose a backend (optional)

Puck is designed to integrate into your existing backend. If you don't already have one or are building a new app, consider Puck Cloud.

Puck Cloud

Puck Cloud is our modular, hosted backend for Puck with a versioned page database, managed authentication, and much more. It's best for when you have no existing backend or database, and is free to start.

To configure it, run the Puck CLI, and select the modules you require:

npx @puckeditor/core init

Pages

Puck Pages is a hosted page store built for Puck, providing version history and data migrations.

npx @puckeditor/core add pages

Auth

Puck Auth provides managed authentication for Puck, allowing users to sign-in with a Puck Cloud account.

npx @puckeditor/core add auth

AI

Puck AI is an AI agent for Puck for generating interfaces directly from the editor.

npx @puckeditor/core add ai

Community

  • Discord server for discussions
  • awesome-puck community repo for plugins, custom fields & more

Get support

If you have any questions about Puck, please open a GitHub issue or join us on Discord.

License

MIT © The Puck Contributors

releases.name: v0.24.0
releases.body:
Puck 0.24 lets you organize fields into groups and tabs, adds checkbox fields, improves drag-and-drop with drag handles, and includes several other API improvements.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70489c1b-4f58-4d05-aebc-3d063800391d

This is a summary of the main new features and full changelog.

**Read the [full release post](https://puckeditor.com/blog/puck-024) on our blog.**

## Summary

- [**Custom field layouts**](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/configuration/component-config#renderfieldsprops): Control how fields are arranged per component using `renderFields`.
- **[Field groups](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/components/field-group) and [tabs](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/components/field-tab):** Organize related fields into collapsible groups or tabs.
- [**Checkbox fields**](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/fields/checkbox): Let users select multiple values from a set of options.
- [**Drag handles**](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/components/action-bar-drag-handle): Make components easier to move in deeply nested layouts.

releases.name: v0.23.0
releases.body:
Puck 0.23 improves drag-and-drop to reduce layout shift, adds a draggable outline for reordering components, and introduces a Dictionary API for translating the editor UI.

[Puck-023.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a35a580f-62a2-4a47-9a49-c73b72e20964)

This is a summary of the main new features and full changelog.

**Read the [full release post](https://puckeditor.com/blog/puck-023) on our blog.**

## Summary

- [**New canvas drag-and-drop**](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/components/puck#behavior): visualize the drop destination using fluid movement or an insertion line.
- [**New outline**](https://puckeditor.com/blog/puck-023#new-outline): reorder, duplicate, and delete components directly from the outline.
- [**Dictionary API**](https://puckeditor.com/docs/api-reference/dictionary): translate or reword every string in the editor UI and switch languages at runtime.

## Full changelog

### Features

* add dictionary ([65790c8](https://github.com/puckeditor/puck/commit/65790c826cfdb51364da14ae9a7d96d43548edae]))
* add draggable outline and streamline UI ([db035ce](https://github.com/puckeditor/puck/commit/db035ce57a94425da9d0e82d3f1c0

aiSummary.oneLiner: Open-source, self-hosted visual editor for React applications that integrates your own components.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Puck is a visual editor specifically built for React. It allows developers to integrate an intuitive drag-and-drop authoring experience directly into their existing applications. Instead of forcing teams into a proprietary ecosystem or headless CMS, Puck uses your own custom React components as its building blocks. This means content creators can visually construct pages using the exact design system developers have already built. It outputs clean JSON data that can be easily rendered, ensuring a strong separation between visual authoring and underlying logic.
keyFeatures: Component integration: Uses your existing custom React components within the visual editor.
Drag and drop interface: Provides an intuitive visual builder for non-technical content authors.
JSON data output: Serializes layouts into clean JSON data for easy storage and rendering.
Inline editing: Allows authors to edit text and properties directly on the visual canvas.
Framework agnostic output: Generates data that can be rendered server-side or client-side.
Self-hosted control: Allows full deployment on your own infrastructure without vendor lock-in.
